items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: I'd like to join the band... Henderson went out to the Greystone and they would come and sit in the Roseland Ballroom

ctx.x: Anyway, I got up there and they had a rehearsal the next morning and they played the "Blue Room" for me and a couple of other things. You know, it was a thrill. Here are things, you write something down and the guys play it. Well, the improvised parts to it, these were the things I was interested in, and they played over things like that and beyond your expectations, you know, lift the whole thing right up. It was a kick.

So what to do. Then I got together and talked with Horvath and Sure, I'd like to join the band. I'd like to do this and do that, and they gave me for that time fairly good pay, and told me that they were on their way into New York to record. This is the way they did. They switched -- Henderson went out to the Greystone and they would come and sit in the Roseland Ballroom and of course, it was always about a day that they would overlap when they were both playing in each place.

"Well, we don't have our numbers picked out yet so just take it easy as much as you can and do whatever you want." It was about two weeks that we would get to the Roseland. So I got acquainted with the guys, that is, Trumbauer and Bix played
